recipes.title: Analyze microscopy slides and three-dimensional scans
recipes.description: Choose by image type and analysis method: interactive segmentation, large-slide annotation, repeatable measurement pipelines or learned classification.

picks.label: Extensible volume workspace
picks.reason: Combines volumetric visualization, segmentation, registration and extensions in one shared environment.
picks.tradeoff: Validate the selected extensions and analysis method for the research workflow; the application does not establish clinical suitability.

picks.label: Focused volume segmentation
picks.reason: Linked orthogonal views and manual or active-contour segmentation suit tracing structures through image volumes.
picks.tradeoff: Its focused toolset offers fewer general-purpose extensions than 3D Slicer; stable and beta packages differ.

picks.label: Whole-slide annotations
picks.reason: Whole-slide viewing, object measurements and interactive classifiers suit microscopy-slide workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Validate classifiers and measurements on representative images; upstream specifies research use.

picks.label: Repeatable batch measurements
picks.reason: Explicit processing pipelines apply the same measurement sequence to many biological images.
picks.tradeoff: Good pipelines still need segmentation tuning and quality checks; Linux uses a separate source-installation route.

picks.label: Interactive image classification
picks.reason: Brush labels train pixel and object classifiers without writing a model-training program.
picks.tradeoff: Training examples determine the result, and GPU packages add hardware and licensing requirements.

recipes.title: Visualize molecules, crystals and particle simulations
recipes.description: Match the viewer to the data: molecular structures and maps, crystallographic densities, teaching demonstrations or particle trajectories.

picks.label: Molecular models with density maps
picks.reason: Combines molecular and volume visualization with commands and extension packages for structural-biology workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Noncommercial and commercial use have different terms; published source is not under an unrestricted open-source license.

picks.label: Scripted molecular figures
picks.reason: Scriptable scenes and molecular representations suit repeatable molecular illustrations.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial application bundles and permissively licensed source have different distribution and support terms.

picks.label: Portable chemistry demonstrations
picks.reason: Java desktop viewing and the related JSmol browser workflow support interactive molecular teaching.
picks.tradeoff: The desktop JAR requires Java; browser embedding is a separate deployment task.

picks.label: Crystals and volume densities
picks.reason: Crystal, polyhedral and isosurface views help inspect structures and density data together.
picks.tradeoff: The redistribution license is restrictive; current terms allow business use at no cost only until business-license conditions are established.

picks.label: Particle and atomistic trajectories
picks.reason: Pipeline-based particle analysis connects structural measurements with simulation visualization.
picks.tradeoff: Basic and Pro expose different modifiers and automation features; large trajectories need suitable resources.

recipes.title: Plot measurements, fit curves and explore mathematics
recipes.description: Choose an interactive plotting application, a scriptable figure generator, a specialist fitter or a broader mathematical environment.

picks.label: Graphical experimental analysis
picks.reason: Worksheets, plots, fitting, data import and digitization support a graphical measurement-analysis workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Notebook backends require separate runtimes; verify fitting models and imported units.

picks.label: Versionable plotting scripts
picks.reason: A compact plotting language produces repeatable two- and three-dimensional figures in automated workflows.
picks.tradeoff: The command language and terminal-specific output settings require learning.

picks.label: Peak and curve fitting
picks.reason: Interactive model construction and fitting tools suit overlapping peaks and experimental curves.
picks.tradeoff: Its published desktop binaries are older than its source release; assess packaging and model assumptions.

picks.label: Numerical engineering and Xcos
picks.reason: Matrix calculations, visualization and block-diagram simulation share one numerical environment.
picks.tradeoff: MATLAB language and toolbox compatibility are incomplete; check each external module.

picks.label: Symbolic and algebraic exploration
picks.reason: A Python-based interface brings algebra, number theory and numerical packages into one mathematical system.
picks.tradeoff: The dependency stack is substantial, and current Windows usage goes through WSL or containers.

recipes.title: Choose a simulation workflow for an engineering problem
recipes.description: Start with the physics and model representation; these tools serve different stages and are often complementary.

picks.label: Equation-based system models
picks.reason: Modelica models and simulation tools suit coupled dynamic systems and reusable component models.
picks.tradeoff: Library compatibility, solver settings and initialization need validation for the chosen model.

picks.label: Interactive electronics learning
picks.reason: A visual real-time circuit environment supports analog, digital and selected microcontroller experiments.
picks.tradeoff: Device models and simulator approximations limit fidelity; check version-specific component support.

picks.label: Biomechanics finite elements
picks.reason: Nonlinear materials and coupled physics focus on biomechanics and biophysics models, with FEBio Studio for model work.
picks.tradeoff: A specialist solver requires validated material models and boundary conditions; source and binary licenses differ.

picks.label: Computational fluid dynamics
picks.reason: The Foundation distribution supplies extensible solvers and utilities for continuum and fluid simulations.
picks.tradeoff: Mesh quality, boundary conditions and solver selection require expertise; Windows and macOS follow supporting-environment instructions.

picks.label: Geometry and simulation meshes
picks.reason: Geometry preparation, meshing and related workflow modules help prepare models for numerical solvers.
picks.tradeoff: A preprocessing platform does not replace the selected solver; module and package compatibility matter.

recipes.title: Process satellite imagery and environmental scenarios
recipes.description: Separate satellite preprocessing, scalable image algorithms, ecosystem-service models and general geographic editing.

picks.label: Sentinel product processing
picks.reason: Mission-specific toolboxes and processing graphs support remote-sensing raster workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Sensor product type and processing order matter; large scenes can require substantial memory and disk space.

picks.label: Scriptable image-processing algorithms
picks.reason: Command-line, Python and QGIS integrations suit repeatable processing of large remote-sensing imagery.
picks.tradeoff: Current package and QGIS-provider versions must match; ARM Mac usage follows a Docker route.

picks.label: Ecosystem-service scenarios
picks.reason: Models connect spatial land-use inputs with ecosystem-service indicators and scenario comparisons.
picks.tradeoff: Outputs depend on local data, assumptions and model scope; inspect the documented telemetry and data requirements.

picks.label: General desktop GIS
picks.reason: Broad vector and raster editing, geoprocessing and map production support the surrounding geographic workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Domain-specific satellite and ecosystem models may still require external tools or plugins.

recipes.title: Build an astronomy acquisition and analysis workflow
recipes.description: Acquisition, mount guiding, plate solving, image processing and time-series measurements are separate jobs that may need several tools.

picks.label: Automated acquisition on Windows
picks.reason: Sequences and supported equipment integrations organize deep-sky imaging sessions.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm the exact camera, focuser, mount and driver support; it is a Windows application.

picks.label: Mount guiding
picks.reason: Guide-star tracking, calibration and diagnostic tools help maintain tracking during exposures.
picks.tradeoff: Guiding cannot compensate for every mechanical or optical problem; the exact guide camera and mount need support.

picks.label: Plate solving and image inspection
picks.reason: Astrometric solving, stacking and FITS tools support image identification and processing.
picks.tradeoff: The selected star database, field of view and input quality affect solving; exact redistribution terms remain unverified.

picks.label: Astronomy image processing
picks.reason: Calibration, registration, stacking and processing tools turn acquired image sets into finished astronomical images.
picks.tradeoff: Correct calibration frames and acquisition metadata remain essential; it does not replace equipment-control software.

picks.label: Photometry and time-series measurements
picks.reason: Astronomy-focused ImageJ tools support calibrated image analysis and light-curve work.
picks.tradeoff: Photometric accuracy depends on calibration, apertures, comparison stars and timing metadata.

recipes.title: Create fonts and manage an installed font collection
recipes.description: Use a font editor to design glyphs and font behavior; use a manager to preview, activate and organize existing typefaces.

picks.label: Open-source font construction
picks.reason: Outline editing, font conversion and scripting cover a broad range of font-authoring tasks.
picks.tradeoff: The dense interface and production settings need learning; validate exports in target shaping and rendering engines.

picks.label: Approachable outline design
picks.reason: Vector glyph editing and common font exports provide a focused font-design workflow.
picks.tradeoff: The free binary edition restricts created fonts to SIL Open Font License output; commercial and advanced formats have separate editions.

picks.label: Commercial typeface production
picks.reason: Detailed glyph, family and variable-font tools target professional font production.
picks.tradeoff: It is paid Windows/macOS software; assess the trial against the required production workflow.

picks.label: Font activation across desktops
picks.reason: Previewing, collections and activation help manage working typeface libraries on Windows, macOS and Linux.
picks.tradeoff: Advanced Awesome features require payment, and application activation behavior needs checking.

picks.label: Linux desktop font management
picks.reason: Font previews, collections and fontconfig-oriented controls serve Linux desktop collections.
picks.tradeoff: Its scope is font management rather than glyph design; desktop and fontconfig behavior affect results.

recipes.title: Program instruments and perform with live code
recipes.description: Choose a beginner-facing live-coding instrument, visual patches or a deeper language for synthesis and precisely timed processes.

picks.label: Approachable live coding
picks.reason: An integrated code editor, samples and synthesis tools support musical programming and performance.
picks.tradeoff: Complex audio routing and custom DSP may require a lower-level environment; web and desktop distributions differ.

picks.label: Visual audio patches
picks.reason: A graphical dataflow model makes control, synthesis and interactive media patches explicit.
picks.tradeoff: External libraries and audio configuration can affect patch portability.

picks.label: Programmable synthesis systems
picks.reason: A language and synthesis server support algorithmic composition, instruments and flexible control.
picks.tradeoff: The language, server architecture and timing model take study.

picks.label: Detailed synthesis instruments
picks.reason: A large opcode library supports explicit signal processing and programmable instruments.
picks.tradeoff: Instrument design and host integration require technical learning; opcode support varies across environments.

picks.label: Precisely timed musical processes
picks.reason: Its strongly timed concurrent language makes timing and live program changes central to musical code.
picks.tradeoff: The timing and concurrency model is distinctive, and additional interfaces may require other tools.

recipes.title: Plan and write a novel, thesis or long document
recipes.description: Choose by working format and planning style: Markdown with citations, structured outlining, story development or a commercial project binder.

picks.label: Markdown research writing
picks.reason: Plain-text files, citation integration and export tools suit research notes and long Markdown documents.
picks.tradeoff: Advanced export depends on the external document toolchain and careful citation configuration.

picks.label: Open-source outlining
picks.reason: An outliner, story-planning tools and focused writing views support structured drafting.
picks.tradeoff: Export capabilities and platform packages differ from commercial writing suites; check the current package for the intended OS.

picks.label: Characters and story structure
picks.reason: Character, scene and narrative-planning tools keep story development alongside manuscript work.
picks.tradeoff: Community and Supporters editions have different features; optional synchronization is a separate service.

picks.label: Commercial project binder
picks.reason: Research material, scenes and draft organization share a project workspace with compilation tools.
picks.tradeoff: Windows and macOS licenses and features differ; learn compilation and backup behavior before a large project.

recipes.title: Translate documents or localize application strings
recipes.description: A translation-memory application fits documents; catalog editors fit software strings and localization formats.

picks.label: Document translation memory
picks.reason: Segmented translation, fuzzy matches, glossaries and translation memories support repeated document work.
picks.tradeoff: Check format filters and final exported documents; it is an assisted translation workflow rather than automatic translation alone.

picks.label: Focused localization editing
picks.reason: Catalog editing and validation support common software and website localization formats.
picks.tradeoff: Paid Pro assistance and services differ from the open-source core; verify the project format and plural rules.

picks.label: Integrated localization workflow
picks.reason: Translation-memory and project tools support sustained application localization work.
picks.tradeoff: Linux is the main desktop route; Windows and macOS installers offered by KDE are nightly testing builds.

recipes.title: Choose software for household books and spending records
recipes.description: Compare bookkeeping structure and import workflow before selecting a tool. Institution connectivity and financial-data formats vary.

picks.label: Double-entry books
picks.reason: Accounts, reconciliation, scheduled transactions and business-oriented records suit structured double-entry bookkeeping.
picks.tradeoff: The accounting model needs learning; online imports and quote services depend on external providers and components.

picks.label: Personal spending analysis
picks.reason: Imports, categories, budgets and reports make household transaction review approachable.
picks.tradeoff: It is oriented toward personal accounts rather than a full business ledger; third-party ports receive limited publisher support.

picks.label: Desktop personal-finance accounts
picks.reason: Account registers, scheduled transactions and reports organize household finances in a KDE application.
picks.tradeoff: Banking plugins vary by platform; the reviewed Windows distribution notes missing AqBanking support.

picks.label: Flexible transaction analysis
picks.reason: Category, tag and report tools support detailed inspection of imported spending records.
picks.tradeoff: Import quality and duplicate handling need review; non-Linux installation routes can require more setup.

recipes.title: Choose accessible input, screen reading and document reading
recipes.description: Match the barrier to the tool: eye-controlled typing, voice commands, desktop speech or accessible reading. Device and application compatibility determine the useful combination.

picks.label: Eye-controlled typing and pointer
picks.reason: An on-screen keyboard and communication tools support interaction through compatible eye trackers and other input methods.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm the exact tracker and OptiKey version; newer releases have changed support for some older hardware.

picks.label: Voice and alternative input
picks.reason: Voice commands, dictation and customizable input actions can support hands-free work across applications.
picks.tradeoff: Commands and recognition require setup and practice; Linux targets X11, and Talon+ has a separate paid membership.

picks.label: Linux desktop speech and braille
picks.reason: Orca exposes accessible desktop interfaces through speech and braille on supported Linux environments.
picks.tradeoff: Results depend on each application exposing a usable accessibility interface.

picks.label: Windows desktop screen reading
picks.reason: The existing NVDA record covers keyboard-driven screen reading and extensibility on Windows.
picks.tradeoff: Application accessibility, speech setup and add-on compatibility require individual checks.

picks.label: Accessible publication reading
picks.reason: Navigation and accessibility support focus on EPUB and other supported digital publications.
picks.tradeoff: Publication structure and protection schemes determine accessible reading; it does not replace a system screen reader.
